dome_favourable_findings_disclosed: Raw H at every dome-cited station sat 13-19 nT below the quiet-day baseline during the eclipse window. Real, reproduced - and matched by ordinary days (2026-08-06, Kp 0.333: -6 to -18 nT).

At both of the dome's global contact times (16:59 and 21:01 UT) H dropped 2-6 nT at NGK, WNG, BEL and LER. On that day's activity level this double coincidence occurs for ~13% of arbitrary time pairs (4.7% on an average control day); it is absent on Z; amplitudes are a quarter or less of the dome's; the r > 0.7 template test does not fire.
NGK's global-contact H fit (-7.8 nT, z -2.5) is within 2 nT of the dome's frozen NGK central (-6.67). One station of seven.
Z-down obscuration-shaped fits at all six priority stations (-2.8 to -7.6 nT). The sign matches the dome's pattern clause; the non-eclipsed ASC shows the same shape (-2.0 to -5.9 nT).
Lagged H fits at EBR and SPT (-8.5 / -8.8 nT at tau 30) sit near the dome's frozen EBR/SPT centrals (-10.66 / -9.82). Hermanus, with no eclipse, gives -8.8 / -9.5 with the same templates.
kernel_of_truth: Two real things sit under the dome's eclipse claims. First, eclipses really do disturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw readings at the dome's stations really were 13-19 nT low - a defender looking only at those numbers would see a hit. Second, the dome's insistence on a quiet-day (Kp<2) precondition is good practice, and this day failed it. Both are true. Neither saves the claim: ordinary days produce the same raw numbers, the dome's own named component shows nothing near its amplitude, its signature contact-phase timing is absent where it would have stood out clearly, and the only eclipse-shaped features we could find also appear at observatories the eclipse never reached. A void test is not a confirmation, and 47 days later the dome's own live scoreboard still reads PENDING.

anticipated_objections.objection: You overrode the dome's Kp<2 precondition - the test was void by its own terms.
anticipated_objections.response: We say so first, in every note. We also void our own Kp-gated criteria. The as-if score uses one quantified rule (DR-1) for both sides; the dome's amplitude and contact-phase signature were 4-25 sigma above that day's noise, while the lower half of our range was not, so the outcomes differ because the amplitudes differ. Operator can choose the standard_physics label instead; we recommend not splitting PRED-095 and TIER-1.

anticipated_objections.objection: The signal is 'umbra-locked' to the global contacts - H dropped at 16:59 and 21:01.
anticipated_objections.response: On H (not the dome's named Z) at 4 northern stations, by 2-6 nT - a quarter of the claimed amplitude. That double coincidence occurs for 13% of arbitrary time pairs on that day's activity. Z shows nothing at either time and the dome's r > 0.7 test fails.

anticipated_objections.objection: Your own post-hoc rules (DR-1, DQ-1, CTL-1) were invented after seeing the data.
anticipated_objections.response: Yes, and we list that as an honest limit. Each rule is applied to both sides, and each was prompted by the adversarial review rather than chosen to rescue a result - DQ-1 removes the only datum that tripped a falsifier of OUR analysis, and CTL-1 removed the eclipse-shaped H fits that would have supported OUR range.

anticipated_objections.objection: Z minima fall within 30 min of maximum coverage at most stations - the 2026-03-15 timing claim is confirmed.
anticipated_objections.response: About half of any +/-60 min window lies within +/-30 min of its centre, so the timing alone is weak; the magnitude clause of the same sentence (-17 to -21 nT) misses by 13+ nT at every priority station.

anticipated_objections.objection: The raw -13 to -19 nT dips are the eclipse.
anticipated_objections.response: The same metric gives -6 to -18 nT on 2026-08-06 (Kp 0.333) and meets the dome-range test on ordinary days; several stations were already at their deepest before the penumbra arrived.
